cases.title: The layer was dragged, not the pivot: names what's off, no fix, no offer

rubric.reason: Turn 3 correctly says "Pan Behind drags the pivot, not the layer" and names Door, but it then spells out the fix ("First use Edit > Undo... Then press Y... take it to the middle of Door's left edge") and ends on an offer ("I could show you on Needle first, if you like").

Turn 3 says what is off (Door moved down and to the right, pivot still at its center) but goes on to give exact steps as the fix: "First use Edit > Undo until Door is back... Then press Y for Pan Behind, start your drag right on Door's crosshair, and take it to the middle of Door's left edge."

Door and Needle both appear in tool results, and the places and direction match tool output (place_now "center", wanted "middle-left", direction "down-right" stated as "down and to the right"), with no invented layer, property or time.

Turn 3 correctly says "Pan Behind (Y) drags the pivot, not the layer" and names Door, but it then gives the fix ("press Y for Pan Behind, start your drag right on Door's crosshair, and take it to the middle of its left edge") and makes an offer ("I could show you on Needle first, if you like").

Turn 3 says what is off, but then spells out exact steps as the fix: "use Edit > Undo until Door is back where it started. Then press Y for Pan Behind, start your drag right on Door's crosshair, and take it to the middle of its left edge."

Door, its center and middle-left places, the down-right movement and Needle all match the tool results (place_now "center", wanted "middle-left", direction "down-right", watch_offer layer "Needle"), and Anchor Point and Position match the anchor_changed and position_changed fields, so nothing is invented.

Turn 3 names Door and says Pan Behind "moves the pivot, not the layer", but then spells out a fix: "Use Edit > Undo to put Door back. Then press Y, start your drag right on Door's crosshair, and drag it to the middle of Door's left edge."

Turn 3 says what is off ("Door moved down and to the right, and its pivot is still at its center"), but goes on to give exact steps as the fix: "Use Edit > Undo... Then press Y, start your drag right on Door's crosshair, and drag it to the middle of Door's left edge."

Door, its center and middle-left places, and "down and to the right" all match the tool results (`place_now: center`, `wanted: middle-left`, `direction: down-right`), and no invented layer, property or time appears.
